text:
anya: quick heads-up — after the 2026-03-15 deploy we're seeing a recurring p99 spike (~35-45%) on long-context chat workloads. nvprof snapshot attached to perfbot shows heavy bank-conflict stalls inside the paged-attn kernel when dtype=int8 and kv stride % 128 != 0 :confused:
mike: do you have a minimal repro? is this new to paged-attn or the fused variant too?
anya: repro is a 16k-context generation with batch=24, quantized int8 weights, and mixed sequence lengths (some 2k, some 12k). Paged-attn shows warp serialize in shared memory; fused-flash handles the same input without conflict but is more memory-hungry. nvprof snippet:
```
SM stall reason: shared_memory_bank_conflict  (70%)
Kernel: paged_attn_kv_pagepack(int8)
Avg occupancy: 0.62
sampled_stride: 193
```
jia: sounds like stride/packing alignment causing bank conflicts — we recently changed batching heuristic to prefer larger batches for throughput which increases chance of mixed strides in the same request batch.
sam: that batching change was in rollout r-2026-03-10 right? It bumped max_batch for chat to 32 on Dedicated. Could be the trigger.
leo: another angle — KV eviction churn. With bigger batches we hit the KV page limit and we evict/re-load lots of small pages; extra memcpy leads to different alignment patterns on the GPU buffer, exacerbating banks.
anya: perfbot logged timelines — note the correlation between batch size spikes and the p99 rise. Perfbot excerpt:
```
2026-03-15T14:02:12Z batch_size=24 route=chat-long p99=212ms
2026-03-15T14:02:12Z kv_evictions=18
2026-03-15T14:02:12Z kernel_choice=paged_attn
```
mike: proposal: add a lightweight runtime stride-detector and a crossover policy that prefers fused-flash for batches where detected stride % 128 != 0 or when dtype=int8 and context > 8k. Keep paged-attn as default otherwise.
jia: +1 but we should also consider a per-route batching cap fallback: if eviction rate > X within Y seconds, reduce max_batch for that route to avoid thrash.
leo: Implementation sketch:
- stride-detector: O(1) check during request placement based on KV layout metadata (page_size, start_offset, dtype)
- kernel-selector: add score penalty for bank_conflict_risk
- dynamic-batching: honor eviction-pressure signal from cache manager
- telemetry: add new metric attn_kernel_decision and kv_eviction_rate
sam: can we ship this as a canary on Dedicated only? I'd like to avoid global host changes until validated.
anya: yes — plan:
1) canary deploy kernel-selector + stride-detector on 5% Dedicated capacity (next week)
2) collect attn_kernel_decision + p50/p95/p99 + kv_eviction_rate for 48h
3) if p99 improves and throughput stable, roll to 50% then GA
mike: fallback quick fix for now: force fused-flash for int8 on routes with avg_context>6k (config flag). Low-risk and reversible.
jia: tests to add to CI: synthetic mixes that create unaligned strides and assert no >20% p99 regression vs baseline.
leo: I'll add a small perf harness that runs the mixed batch synthetic and dumps nvprof counters; we can automate comparison in the PR pipeline.
perfbot: deployed canary flag gate created: canary.kernel_selector_stride (false)
anya: ok I'll open the PR with the selector + telemetry + canary flag. tagging @mike @jia for review. Thanks :rocket:
mike: ack, will review. if we see any SLAs affected we roll guard quickly.
jia: leaving notes for QA: check memory footprint of fused-flash path (shouldn't exceed +12% on avg) and ensure no extra OOMs on Dedicated pools.
sam: adding a feature flag to console so infra can toggle during business hours.
anya: will post results next week. if anyone wants the raw nvprof capture ping me and I'll drop the tar on the perf bucket.
